§3§lPurpose and mechanism§r
Use the bronze-tier Heavy Steam Turbine to turn ordinary steam into electricity. This compact, independent generator cannot be stacked. Bronze and steel structures use the same controller; the uniform structure material determines the tier. This quest checks for one controller in your inventory §2without consuming it§r. Possession does not prove that a bronze structure is built, generating or at full efficiency.

§3§lPreparation and operation§r
Follow the current projection, using bronze material casings, pipes, gearboxes and frames with ordinary glass. Hatches can replace ordinary bronze casing positions; install at least one steam input, one fluid output and one dynamo. No maintenance hatch is needed. Supply ordinary steam: bronze cannot use superheated steam. Connect distilled-water recovery and a suitable electrical destination; every §1160 L§r of ordinary steam yields §11 L§r of distilled water. Ordinary, multi-amp and laser dynamos are supported, but supply, dynamo throughput and free energy storage, and fluid-outlet space limit the actual load.

§3§lFlow and efficiency§r
Bronze is rated for §1512 L/t§r of ordinary steam and produces §1256 EU/t§r at rated flow and §1100%§r efficiency; its efficiency cap is §1125%§r. Cold-start efficiency is §10%§r, gaining §12§r percentage points per accumulated operating second up to §1100%§r even with limited supply. Above that, continuous rated flow and sufficient dynamo/output space are required to gain §11§r percentage point per second. Partial load limits effective efficiency to §1100%§r and lowers output with actual steam use; each tick discards fractions below §11 EU§r. Start with stable input and recovery, then increase flow. A later steel rebuild uses the same controller and different operating ratings.
